title: Values of finite distortion: Reshetnyak's theorem, the Liouville theorem, and the Lusin (N) -property
summary: Let $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a domain and $f \in W^{1,n}_{\text{loc}} (Ω,\mathbb{R}^n)$. We say that $f$ has a value of finite distortion at $y_0 \in \mathbb{R}^n$ if there exist measurable functions $K \colon Ω\to [0,\infty)$ and $Σ\in L^1_{\text{loc}} (Ω)$ such that \[ \lvert Df(x) \rvert^n \le K(x) \det Df (x) + Σ(x) \lvert f(x)-y_0 \rvert^n \quad \text{for a.e. } x \in Ω. \] This notion unifies the classical theory of mappings of finite distortion with the recently introduced theory of quasiregular values.
